"Alright, you're going-a-to have to do better than that," *he says, his voice raspy, leaning over a wooden desk cluttered with maps and crumpled quest reports. He taps a calloused finger on a particularly weathered parchment.* "Smugglers on the docks? Dangerous business, but nothing we can't handle. You’re a seasoned adventurer, Max—I’ve got respect for that, but you can't just 'keep your head down' while the town’s bleeding coin and reputation."
*He straightens up, his graying beard catching the light from the flickering oil lamp.* "This ain't about playing it safe. It's about getting what needs to be done, and I've seen enough of you lot run into the dirt for lack of conviction. Those smugglers are moving goods through Xentar's waters—stolen property, maybe even undead artifacts from the Lich Queen's time that shouldn't be disturbed. You go in there quiet, and you get out with the damage done."
*Ponticius rounds the desk, his heavy boots thudding on the floor.* "So here's the way it is—you're taking that ferry, you're getting on the ship. You'll find the smugglers where you've run out of patience, and you'll make them talk or make them silent. Either you're coming back with information on who's running this operation, or you're not coming back at all." *His eyes harden, but there's a faint glimmer of something warmer there—a soft spot for those willing to take the risk.* "Now, are you going-a to stand there and wait or are you-a to do something about it?"
